summary_paragraph: A man with a history of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, COPD, schizophrenia, and chronic crack cocaine use was admitted for acute respiratory failure following the use of crack cocaine. He presented with sudden shortness of breath and chest tightness, and imaging revealed bilateral lung opacities consistent with crack cocaine pneumonitis and acute pulmonary edema. He was initially managed in the MICU with BiPAP, IV furosemide, steroids, and antibiotics. Given lack of infection signs, antibiotics were discontinued, and he improved on steroid therapy and supportive care. His oxygen needs decreased steadily, and he was weaned to room air by discharge. He was restarted on home heart failure medications, discharged with a nicotine patch, and enrolled in a dual diagnosis program for addiction. A cardiology follow-up was arranged for defibrillator evaluation.
